_schema: world size (as a string) -> the measured peak for that world. A key exists only if a run at THAT world size reported it; extrapolating from another world is what gate_memory_measured refuses.
_caveat: Every peak here is RANK 0 (train.py's log line is is_main), so each is a LOWER bound on the worst rank -- per-rank DDP buckets differ. Safe to rule from at 25 GiB of headroom; NOT safe below about 10 GiB, where every rank has to report before the number means anything.
_why_not_nvidia_smi: nvidia-smi reads the caching allocator's reservation, not the high-water mark of live tensors. It returned 74.10 GiB at world=3 and 74.09 at world=7 -- the DDP bucket growth these measurements exist to find is invisible to it, because a larger bucket is served from cache the allocator never returns. Every fits/does-not-fit call in this repo before train.py:2604 (661e5ce) came from that number.

8.note: A BY-PRODUCT of the crash-recovery gate test, not a measurement run: that test trains 60 steps and is killed at 40, so this reading comes from a job that was deliberately terminated. The kill is unrelated to the peak -- it happened after step 40 reported, and the figure had already been flat across four windows by then, one more than the world=7 entry. Recorded because the shape is the launch recipe exactly (mix_500m, all nine domains, same batch/accum/depth/precision) and re-running a dedicated 30-step probe would measure the same thing twice. Identical to world=7's 69.63: per-card activations do not move when a rank is added, which is what DDP predicts and what this now shows rather than assumes.

7_alt_b16a2.config: b16 accum2 -- same 917,504 tok/step as b32 accum1, half the activation set
7_alt_b16a2.role: control, not fallback. Its purpose was to prove the peak field tracks configuration at all -- the prediction that it must read materially lower was recorded in eff.w7_peak_memory_b32_fits before this arm ran. It is also the reserve: where 33 GiB comes from if seq or mix complexity grows.

_model.predicted_from: 493.6M params x 2 bytes x 3 copies (weights + Muon momentum + grads); agreement to 0.19 GiB is what makes this a model rather than a two-point fit
_model.note: Peak is LINEAR in batch. A first reading that grad_ckpt made activations sub-linear was wrong. Extrapolations from this line assume activation memory scales with seq the way it scales with batch, which is UNTESTED -- attention's quadratic term and the KDA recurrent state need not move together. On that assumption seq 8192 puts b32 at ~136 GiB (does not fit) and b16a2 at ~70 GiB (fits), making b32 the ceiling for this card at seq 4096.

4.config: b16 accum2 d1024 L12 h8 ffn3072 seq4096 NO grad_ckpt fp8=True attn_res-Full/0 doc_mask -- the LAUNCHED configuration
4.steps: measured live on the launched run, steps 10/20/30
4.source: MEASURED ON THE LEG ITSELF. This replaces the 61.01 GiB I recorded before launch, which was read off the A/B (2a) baseline arm as a same-shape reuse. The shape matched and the recipe matched flag for flag, but the DTYPE did not: run_ddp.sh:74 passes --fp8, and that arm was launched by scripts/run_ab_speedrun.sh, which calls torchrun directly and does not. Its log says `fp8 False`, this run's says `fp8 True`.
4.range_over_50_windows: 60.95 - 61.01 GiB, spread 0.06 GiB (8/16/14/8/3/1 windows at 60.95/.96/.97/.98/.99/61.01). The MAX is recorded, not the mean or the modal value -- a fits/does-not-fit call is made against the worst window, and the mean would understate it by 0.05 GiB.
4.mix_difference_is_not_a_memory_differenc: The arm ran data/mix_200m_4b.json and the leg runs data/mix_200m_8b.json. Checked rather than waved past: same 9 domains, and all 9 weight deltas are exactly 0.0 -- the two files differ only in total_tokens (3,999,997,952 vs 8,000,000,000), which sets how many steps run, not what one step allocates. Peak is a per-step high-water mark.
4._caveat_applies: Rank 0 only, like every other row here, so this is a LOWER bound on the worst rank. The file's own rule is that ruling from it needs about 25 GiB of headroom; 34.57 GiB clears that. It clears it by less than the 493.6M/b16a2 arm's 58.93 GiB, because this leg runs WITHOUT grad_ckpt -- 206M unchecked costs more activation memory than 493.6M checkpointed.

superseded_reuse.why_it_was_wrong: I checked params, world, batch, accum, seq, grad_ckpt, lr_scale, attn_every and the mix's nine weights, and did not check fp8. The arm's own header printed `fp8 False` in the line above the cfg line I read, so the evidence was on screen and I matched on the fields I had thought to list.
superseded_reuse.direction: OVER by 11.48 GiB (23%). The reuse was conservative, so the fits/does-not-fit call it licensed was not endangered -- but that is luck about the sign, not a property of the method. Had fp8 cost memory instead of saving it, the same procedure would have licensed a launch that OOMs.
superseded_reuse.rule: A same-shape peak reuse must enumerate the DTYPE and the LAUNCHER, not only the model and recipe flags. Two launchers for one shape (run_ddp.sh appends --fp8, run_ab_speedrun.sh calls torchrun directly and does not) differ in what reaches argv, and the reused number was measured under the other one. AND THE SAME UNCHECKED FIELD BROKE A SECOND METRIC THE SAME HOUR: MFU. train.py:2242 sets peak_tflops = 296 if fp8 else 148 (H20 FP8 vs bf16), so this leg's 34% and the anchor arm's 48% are ratios against denominators that differ 2x. Actual throughput is 82K vs 56K tok/s/gpu -- 1.46x FASTER at the lower MFU, and 68.5% if scored on the anchor's bf16 peak. MFU IS NOT COMPARABLE ACROSS DTYPES because its denominator is a function of dtype; tok/s is. One unenumerated field, two metrics, wrong both times -- once predicting memory from a non-fp8 run, once comparing an fp8 run's efficiency to a non-fp8 one.

_probe_b8_d1024_w1.config: b8 accum1 d1024 L12 h8 ffn3072 seq4096 NO grad_ckpt fp8=True world=1 -- CONTROL for the d-scaling probe, not a launch candidate
_probe_b8_d1024_w1.card: 5, granted by 6e 08:24:06Z; read 0 MiB at 08:30:39Z before the claim
_probe_b8_d1024_w1.role: CONTROL. Its job was to be able to FAIL: it tests whether activations scale with the FORWARD batch (predict 25.43) or with the effective batch, i.e. accum counted too (predict 13.39). Measured 24.08 -- 1.36 from the first, 10.69 from the second, a factor of 7.9. So forward batch is the axis. A probe that could only confirm would have proved nothing.
_probe_b8_d1024_w1.residual_explained_by: MISLABELLED IF CALLED 'the world=4 overhead'. 2.710 = the leg (world4 b16 accum2) minus 2 x this probe (world1 b8 accum1), so it is a RESIDUAL containing the world effect, the accum difference, and anything else unaccounted. It must NOT be scaled as a function of world size. The direction is still informative -- 2 x A8 = 45.48 < the leg's A16 = 48.19, and miscounting accum would have given the opposite sign or an order of magnitude, not 5.3% -- but the decomposition is not measured. Separating it needs the same shape at world=1 and world=4, which the full-batch launch gate will supply for free.
_probe_b8_d1024_w1.why_the_ratio_and_not_the_absolute: d-scaling is read from probe/probe (same world, launcher, dtype and accum, so those cancel). The ABSOLUTE peak for the params leg still needs a world=4 full-batch --peak-only: the world=4 overhead is present there and absent here, and no ratio recovers it. The two measurements are not substitutes.
_probe_b8_d1024_w1.compile_transient_note: nvidia-smi read 72,566 MiB on card 5 during the d1536 arm's compile phase. That is NOT in any peak_GiB here: profile_step_cost.py:576 resets the counter under `if st == a.warmup`, so every number in this file is the STEADY-STATE step. A compile transient OOMs just as hard, and it is unmeasured. Do not read a peak here as 'this shape will start'.
_probe_b8_d1024_w1.why_the_leading_underscore: gate_memory_measured (scripts/launch_gate.py:560) reports every key NOT starting with '_' as a world size we have a measured peak for. This is a b8 world=1 PROBE, not a peak for any launch: listing it bare would tell a reader 'world=1 is measured' and, worse, invite the same reuse-by-shape that put 61.01 in this file. The underscore keeps it out of that list while keeping the measurement auditable.

_probe_b8_d1536_w1.config: b8 accum1 d1536 L12 h12 ffn4608 seq4096 NO grad_ckpt fp8=True world=1 -- the d-scaling probe's TEST arm, paired with _probe_b8_d1024_w1. Not a peak for any launch.
_probe_b8_d1536_w1.shape_confirmed_by: the log's `built 438.36M params` line: 438,363,756 occurs only at d1536 L12 h12 ffn4608, and it is printed AFTER the model is constructed, so it certifies the shape took effect. A flag is set before construction and can be silently ignored.
_probe_b8_d1536_w1.card: 5, granted by 6e 08:24:06Z; read 0 MiB at 08:35:51Z before the claim
_probe_b8_d1536_w1.how_the_exponent_was_solved: A = reserved - P, where P (params+grads+Muon momentum+AdamW fp32 states) is computed from the instantiated model, NOT fitted: 1.340 GiB at d1024, 2.732 at d1536. Then exponent = ln(A1536/A1024)/ln(1.5) = ln(33.828/22.740)/ln(1.5) = 0.9795. P MUST be subtracted first: it is an ADDITIVE term, not a common factor. Taking the raw ratio of the two readings gives 1.0299, biased +0.050, which reads as 'above 1' when the answer is below it.
_probe_b8_d1536_w1.projection_to_the_params_leg: A(d1536,b16) = 33.828 x 2 = 67.66, so b16 world=4 lands at 73.10 GiB if the leg-minus-probe residual (2.710) is constant, or 76.15 if it scales with params (x2.128). Both fit in 95.22 with 19-22 GiB spare, so that ambiguity needs no resolving at this exponent.
_probe_b8_d1536_w1.what_this_does_NOT_answer: the absolute peak of the params leg. This is world=1; the launch is world=4, whose NCCL buffers and DDP bucket are absent here and cannot be recovered from a ratio. A full-batch world=4 --peak-only remains the launch gate. Also unmeasured: the compile transient, which read 72,566 MiB on nvidia-smi during THIS arm's compile phase while the steady-state number above is 36.56 -- profile_step_cost.py:576 resets the counter at `st == a.warmup` by design, so nothing in this file says whether a shape will START.
_probe_b8_d1536_w1.cost: two single-card probes, ~4 minutes each, no block time

unverified_transfers.batch_linearity_at_d1536: SUPERSEDED BY MEASUREMENT, see _probe_b16_d1536_w1. This entry projected b8 -> b16 by doubling and predicted 70.39 GiB; the measured value is 72.12, so A(b16)/A(b8) = 2.0512, not 2.000. Batch is slightly super-linear and the 2.6% error was in the UNSAFE direction. The original note (kept below) said it would take a 33% error to overturn 'fits' -- true, and still true -- but it also called batch linearity the hardest assumption in the stack, and the sign of its error was not anticipated. ORIGINAL: b8 -> b16 doubling uses linearity MEASURED AT d1024 (_model, from b16 and b32); applying it at d1536 is a transfer, not a measurement.
unverified_transfers.the_2710_residual: see _probe_b8_d1024_w1.residual_explained_by: it is a residual, not a world=4 overhead, and it would take 24.8 GiB -- 9.2x its size -- to overturn the conclusion.
unverified_transfers.why_stated_and_not_verified: a conclusion with 19-22 GiB of headroom can leave its assumptions unverified; it cannot leave them unstated. Each one here is recorded with how far it is from flipping the answer.

_probe_b16_d1536_w1.config: b16 accum2 d1536 L12 h12 ffn4608 seq4096 NO grad_ckpt fp8=True world=1 -- the params leg's OWN batch and accum, every field matching the leg except world
_probe_b16_d1536_w1.card: 6; read-and-launch were ONE command (nvidia-smi read 0 MiB at 08:51:30Z, then a `< 1000 MiB` test gated the launch in the same shell line). Card 5 had been taken by another process within seconds of a release earlier, so read-then-decide has no window.
_probe_b16_d1536_w1.why_this_one_exists: it is the world=1 counterpart of the launch gate's world=4 reading. Every field except world matches, so gate_reading - 72.12 isolates the world=4 overhead with no extra card time -- which is what _probe_b8_d1024_w1's 2.710 residual could not do, since it also carried a batch and accum difference.
_probe_b16_d1536_w1.supersedes_the_projection: the earlier b8 -> b16 doubling predicted 70.39 GiB and MEASURED is 72.12: A(b16)/A(b8) = 69.388/33.828 = 2.0512, not 2.000. Batch is slightly SUPER-linear, and the 2.6% error was in the unsafe direction -- the projection under-predicted memory. It was recorded as needing a 33% error to overturn 'fits', which still holds, but the SIGN was not anticipated and the note called batch linearity the hardest assumption in the stack. It is the hardest and it is still not exact.
_probe_b16_d1536_w1.no_compile_spike_at_this_batch: STARTUP 71.95 is 0.17 GiB BELOW the steady 72.12, so at b16 there is no compile transient above steady state. This REFUTES the prediction that this shape would OOM during compile, which came from reading the b8 arm's nvidia-smi 70.87 GiB as a compile transient: at b8 the nvidia-smi/torch-reserved gap was 34.31 GiB, at b16 it is 1.19 GiB. A transient scaling with the shape cannot shrink as the shape doubles. The gap was the caching allocator holding freed blocks (nvidia-smi counts the whole process, torch reserved counts its pool); at b16 nearly all of the pool is live, so the two converge. SCOPE: this says nothing about other shapes or batches -- only that this one has no startup spike.
_probe_b16_d1536_w1.params_leg_projection: world=4 = 72.12 + the world overhead, still the one unmeasured term: 74.83 GiB if 2.710 is constant, 77.89 if it scales with params. Both fit in 95.22 with 17-20 GiB spare, now on a MEASURED b16 base rather than a doubled b8 one.
